### VerifyOptions {#VerifyOptions}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag">interface</span> <code class="sdk-qual">cluster.VerifyOptions</code></div>

Clients for contract-wallet (EIP-1271) definition signatures, such as a
Safe creator. The SDK has no RPCs of its own (2.x had built-in ones): pass
`publicClients` by chain id (a server that verifies several chains), or a
`publicClient` on the definition's chain. Without a client for that chain,
a signature that does not recover to its signer is reported as
unverifiable (`signature_unverifiable`, `definition_signature_unverifiable`)
rather than checked.

```ts sdk-signature
interface VerifyOptions extends SignatureClients {
  publicClient?: PublicClient;
}
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>publicClient?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">PublicClient</span> | For signatures on its own chain only; one on another chain is ignored. |
| <code>publicClients?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./checks#PublicClients">PublicClients</a></span> | Clients by chain id, for a caller that checks signatures of several chains (a server). |

</div>

<p class="sdk-see"><a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/src/cluster/verifyDefinition.ts#L41">source</a></p>

### LockVerificationLevel {#LockVerificationLevel}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag">type</span> <code class="sdk-qual">cluster.LockVerificationLevel</code></div>

- `full`: every step, every BLS check.
- `attested`: the checks that need no BLS work: definition flow and
  signatures, hashes, share layout, deposit and builder registration
  fields, node signatures; plus the BLS signatures of the deposits and
  builder registrations of the validators in `signatures`. Charon verifies
  every BLS signature during the DKG before each node signs `lock_hash`, so
  valid node signatures over a matching `lock_hash` attest to them.

```ts sdk-signature
type LockVerificationLevel = 'attested' | 'full';
```

<p class="sdk-see"><a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/src/cluster/verifyLock.ts#L79">source</a></p>

### VerifyLockOptions {#VerifyLockOptions}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag">interface</span> <code class="sdk-qual">cluster.VerifyLockOptions</code></div>

```ts sdk-signature
interface VerifyLockOptions {
  publicClient?: PublicClient;
  publicClients?: PublicClients;
  level?: LockVerificationLevel;
  signatures?: 'all' | 'none' | number[];
  yieldMs?: number;
  bls?: BlsBackend;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>publicClient?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">PublicClient</span> | A client for contract-wallet (EIP-1271) definition signatures, such as a Safe creator: used for a lock on its own chain only. The SDK has no RPCs of its own (2.x had built-in ones). See `publicClients`. |
| <code>publicClients?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./checks#PublicClients">PublicClients</a></span> | Clients by chain id (or a function of the chain id), for a caller that verifies locks of several chains: the one for the lock's chain (from its `fork_version`) checks contract-wallet signatures. Without a client for that chain, a definition signature that does not recover to its signer fails as `definition_signature_unverifiable`. |
| <code>level?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="#LockVerificationLevel">LockVerificationLevel</a></span> | Default `full`. |
| <code>signatures?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">'all' &#124; 'none' &#124; number[]</span> | Validators (indexes in the lock) whose deposit and builder registration BLS signatures `attested` checks: `all`, `none` (default) or a list. `full` checks all of them (only `all` is accepted with it). |
| <code>yieldMs?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">number</span> | Longest stretch of work, in ms, between yields to the event loop (default 50; 0 = never yield). A stretch can overrun it by one unit of work (one signature, about 25 ms with the default backend). |
| <code>bls?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./checks#BlsBackend">BlsBackend</a></span> | BLS backend (default `nobleBls`, pure JavaScript). |
| <code>signal?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">AbortSignal</span> | Aborts the verification: checked at every yield point (between units of work), and an abort throws [`ABORTED`](../../errors.md#ABORTED) with the signal's reason as `cause`. The way for a server to bound the CPU spent per request, e.g. `AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)`. With `yieldMs: 0` the event loop never runs during the call, so a timer cannot fire mid-run. |

</div>

<p class="sdk-see"><a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/src/cluster/verifyLock.ts#L93">source</a></p>

### ClusterModule {#ClusterModule}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag">interface</span> <code class="sdk-qual">cluster.ClusterModule</code></div>

The cluster module bound to a client context. `verifyDefinition` defaults
`chainId` to the client chain, and the verifiers use the client's
`publicClient` for contract-wallet signatures on the client chain, after
any `publicClient` / `publicClients` the options pass.

```ts sdk-signature
interface ClusterModule {
  computeConfigHash: typeof computeConfigHash;
  computeDefinitionHash: typeof computeDefinitionHash;
  computeLockHash: typeof computeLockHash;
  prepareDefinition: (
    input: BoundDefinitionInput,
  ) => PreparedDefinition;
  create: (
    input:
      | PreparedDefinition
      | (Omit<BoundDefinitionInput, 'creator'> & {
          creator?: string;
        }),
  ) => Promise<Hex>;
  accept: (input: {
    configHash: string;
    enr: string;
    version?: string;
  }) => Promise<ClusterDefinition>;
  get: (configHash: string) => Promise<ClusterDefinition>;
  getLock: (
    input:
      | {
          configHash: string;
        }
      | {
          lockHash: string;
        },
  ) => Promise<ClusterLock>;
  watch: (
    configHash: string,
    options: WatchOptions,
  ) => AsyncIterable<ClusterEvent>;
  verifyDefinition: (
    input: {
      definition: unknown;
      configHash?: string;
      chainId?: number;
    },
    options?: VerifyOptions,
  ) => Promise<DefinitionVerification>;
  verifyLock: (
    lock: unknown,
    options?: VerifyLockOptions,
  ) => Promise<LockVerification>;
  isValidLock: (
    lock: unknown,
    options?: VerifyLockOptions,
  ) => Promise<boolean>;
}
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>computeConfigHash</code> | <span class="sdk-type">typeof computeConfigHash</span> |  |
| <code>computeDefinitionHash</code> | <span class="sdk-type">typeof computeDefinitionHash</span> |  |
| <code>computeLockHash</code> | <span class="sdk-type">typeof computeLockHash</span> |  |
| <code>prepareDefinition</code> | <span class="sdk-type">(input: <a href="#BoundDefinitionInput">BoundDefinitionInput</a>) =&gt; <a href="#PreparedDefinition">PreparedDefinition</a></span> | As the pure `prepareDefinition`; `chainId` defaults to the client chain. |
| <code>create</code> | <span class="sdk-type">( input: &#124; <a href="#PreparedDefinition">PreparedDefinition</a> &#124; (Omit&lt;<a href="#BoundDefinitionInput">BoundDefinitionInput</a>, 'creator'&gt; &amp; { creator?: string }), ) =&gt; Promise&lt;Hex&gt;</span> | Takes what `prepareDefinition` returned, or its input (then `creator` defaults to the wallet account and `chainId` to the client chain). |
| <code>accept</code> | <span class="sdk-type">(input: { configHash: string; enr: string; version?: string; }) =&gt; Promise&lt;<a href="#ClusterDefinition">ClusterDefinition</a>&gt;</span> | Joins a cluster as an operator: fetches the definition, verifies it (`verifyDefinition`, else DEFINITION_INVALID), checks the wallet account is one of its operators (ACCOUNT_NOT_OPERATOR), then signs the config hash and the ENR and posts them. Accepting again with the same ENR returns the definition without signing. |
| <code>get</code> | <span class="sdk-type">(configHash: string) =&gt; Promise&lt;<a href="#ClusterDefinition">ClusterDefinition</a>&gt;</span> | The cluster definition for `configHash` from the Obol API. Not verified: pass it to `verifyDefinition` before acting on it. A file for another hash: API_RESPONSE_MISMATCH. |
| <code>getLock</code> | <span class="sdk-type">( input: { configHash: string } &#124; { lockHash: string }, ) =&gt; Promise&lt;<a href="#ClusterLock">ClusterLock</a>&gt;</span> | The cluster lock by `configHash` or `lockHash` from the Obol API (API_NOT_FOUND until the DKG has published it). Not verified: use `verifyLock`, or [`deposits.fromLock`](../deposits.md#fromLock), which verifies by default. |
| <code>watch</code> | <span class="sdk-type">( configHash: string, options: <a href="#WatchOptions">WatchOptions</a>, ) =&gt; AsyncIterable&lt;<a href="#ClusterEvent">ClusterEvent</a>&gt;</span> | Follows a definition until its lock is published: yields `operator_signed` once per newly signed operator, `definition_ready` once, then `lock_published` and ends. Polls every `intervalMs` (default 12 s) and backs off on rate limits; aborting `signal` ends the iteration without an error. |
| <code>verifyDefinition</code> | <span class="sdk-type">( input: { definition: unknown; configHash?: string; chainId?: number }, options?: <a href="#VerifyOptions">VerifyOptions</a>, ) =&gt; Promise&lt;<a href="#DefinitionVerification">DefinitionVerification</a>&gt;</span> |  |
| <code>verifyLock</code> | <span class="sdk-type">( lock: unknown, options?: <a href="#VerifyLockOptions">VerifyLockOptions</a>, ) =&gt; Promise&lt;<a href="#LockVerification">LockVerification</a>&gt;</span> |  |
| <code>isValidLock</code> | <span class="sdk-type">(lock: unknown, options?: <a href="#VerifyLockOptions">VerifyLockOptions</a>) =&gt; Promise&lt;boolean&gt;</span> |  |
